notes: The guard on the moved row is probabilistic on this pod. With the effect keyed on the `highlight` object again (the regression the memo fixed), the row passed 40 of 40 in chromium, where the implementer measured 2 of 40 and round 3 of sjawhar/legion#2472 measured 5 of 40 on the unfixed view. The mutation is the real regression: VersionView.test.tsx's 'keeps its editor when the parent renders again with an equal highlight' fails under it with editors 2 (expected 1) and passes once restored. So the deterministic lock on that fix is the unit test, and the browser row is the slower, machine-dependent one; this change strengthens that row rather than weakening it, and nothing here asks for a change.

The new fall rule is stronger than the exact-zero filter everywhere this row can reach: the only case the old rule caught and the new one does not is a fall to 0 from a peak of 64 px or less, which cannot happen on a page whose landing offset is about 1980 px and whose quote must end in the viewport.

Comment claims checked against the code: ProofDocument.tsx:918-923 renders VersionView and forwards `highlight`, and ArtifactDocument.tsx:59-70 builds that object afresh on every render, so VersionView.tsx's rewritten comment is true of the parents it names.

The handoff commit d5154340 differs from the code head 71c76b62 only by .legion/INFRA-728/implement.json, so every run above tested the code at both; its message carries `skip-checks: true` as the last line after two empty lines.
